children.text: Replace this photo: the dojo, outside or inside. Open Edit layout at the top left and drop a photo on this frame. You can change the text there too.
A dojo for children through to adults. Manners, consideration, and the habit of coming back are part of the training.
Fitness and self-defence are in the class. So is the kind of person the training is meant to make.
From the children's class to adults and seniors
Gradings, and competition if you want it
You can watch, or join a session
Classes by age and by level.
Replace this photo from Edit layout at the top left. Drop a photo on this frame, and edit the text there too. Photo idea: children practising a basic form.
Manners and the basic movements, taught so children can enjoy them. Focus and confidence come with that.
Replace this photo from Edit layout at the top left. Drop a photo on this frame, and edit the text there too. Photo idea: adults in sparring or forms.
Basics, sparring, and forms. A way to train, and a way to get moving again.
Replace this photo from Edit layout at the top left. Drop a photo on this frame, and edit the text there too. Photo idea: women or older members training.
Fitness and self-defence, at a pace that doesn't ask you to keep up with the teenagers.
What this dojo keeps at the centre
A greeting, thanks, and some consideration for the person in front of you. The bow at the start and the end is how that is practised.
Getting a little better, and learning how to come back next week.
Fitness, and also a steadier mind and better judgment.

Questions people ask before they join.
I've never really trained. Is that a problem?
Yes. A first class starts from the basics.
How old do you need to be?
Do I need a gi for the first class?
Not for a trial. Wear something you can move in.
No. Competition is optional. We'll help if you want it.
Come and watch, or come and try a class.
